```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(sf)
  library(leaflet)
  library(knitr)
})

out_dir <- "output/unified"
geo_out <- "geocoding/output"
geo_in  <- "geocoding/input"

read_data <- function(filename, dir = out_dir) {
  read_csv(file.path(dir, filename), show_col_types = FALSE)
}

# The page's one helper: the lines of `file` from the first line containing
# `from` up to, not including, the next line containing `to`. Every code block
# on this page is pulled from the scripts through it at render time.
excerpt <- function(file, from, to) {
  lines <- readLines(file, encoding = "UTF-8", warn = FALSE)
  start <- grep(from, lines, fixed = TRUE)[1]
  if (is.na(start)) stop("Anchor not found in ", file, ": ", from)
  end <- start + grep(to, lines[-seq_len(start)], fixed = TRUE)[1]
  if (is.na(end)) stop("Anchor not found in ", file, " after '", from, "': ", to)
  out <- lines[start:(end - 1)]
  out[seq_len(max(which(nzchar(trimws(out)))))]
}

# The geocoding configuration, read as data: config.R only defines lists.
cfg <- new.env()
sys.source("geocoding/pipeline/config.R", envir = cfg)

pairs_in <- read_data("drc_dps_site_pairs.csv", geo_in)
net_size <- with(count(pairs_in, network), setNames(n, network))
n_old_provinces <- n_distinct(pairs_in$province[pairs_in$network == "2003_2005"])

missing_2021 <- read_csv(
  "output/network_51/missing_2021_site.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)$dps_province

journeys <- read_data("Table_assigned_travel_times.csv")
routes   <- read_data("walking_route_distances.csv")
coverage <- read_data("Table_spatial_accessibility_summary.csv")
validation <- read_data("Table_accessibility_validation.csv")
model_cfg <- read_data("accessibility_model_configuration.csv")
```

How long does it take a Provincial Health Division (*Division Provinciale de la Santé*, **DPS**) team to reach the malaria entomological sentinel sites it supervises in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and how much of the country lies within reach of a site? We answer both questions for three successive configurations of the national network, all under the same 2020 travel-time surfaces:

- **2003–2005:** the `r net_size[["2003_2005"]]` historical sites, under the old `r n_old_provinces`-province map.
- **2014:** `r net_size[["2014"]]` sites, one per province.
- **2021 proposal:** the `r net_size[["2014"]]` existing sites plus `r net_size[["2021_expansion"]]` proposed ones, `r net_size[["2014"]] + net_size[["2021_expansion"]]` in all. `r missing_2021` has no 2021 site.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" icon="false" title="How to read this page"}
Every stage follows the same order: **Why** → **Where it lives** → **Code** → **Result**. Pipeline code is folded: click *Show code*, or use **</> Code → Show All Code** at the top right. Each code block is pulled from the script at render time, so it is the code that actually ran. Nothing on this page runs the pipeline. The page reads the saved outputs, and every number is computed from them.

# Site registry {#sec-registry}

**Why.** Before anything can be mapped, we need one list of which health zones served as sentinel sites in each period. The source workbook lists the original sites under the pre-2015 provinces and the 2014 additions under the new ones. The extractor therefore relabels the original sites onto the post-2015 provinces before combining the two lists, and stops if the result is not exactly one site per province.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false" title="Where it lives"}
- **Script:** `extract_sentinel_sites_26.py` (Python)
- **Reads:** `data/input/DRC_Health_Zones_Sentinel_Sites.xlsx`, sheet `Metadata`: the original sites (A3:B13) and the 2014 additions (D3:E17)
- **Writes:** `geocoding/input/drc_sentinel_sites_26.csv`
- **Second input:** `geocoding/input/drc_sentinel_sites_2021_expansion.csv`, the sites selected in 2021 (sheet `2021_expansion` of `data/input/DRC_DPS.xlsx`)
- **Network membership:** `geocoding/input/drc_dps_site_pairs.csv`
:::

```{python}
#| eval: false
#| python.reticulate: false
#| filename: "extract_sentinel_sites_26.py"
#| code: !expr 'c(excerpt("extract_sentinel_sites_26.py", "CROSSWALK_2015 = {", "FIELDNAMES ="), "", "# ⋯", "", excerpt("extract_sentinel_sites_26.py", "# Structural guard on CROSSWALK_2015", "sites = [r["))'
```

**Result.** The three networks as the pipeline reads them (no coordinates yet):

```{r}
#| label: registry
#| code-summary: "How this table is built"

registry <- bind_rows(
  read_data("drc_sentinel_sites_26.csv", geo_in) |>
    mutate(file = "drc_sentinel_sites_26.csv"),
  read_data("drc_sentinel_sites_2021_expansion.csv", geo_in) |>
    mutate(file = "drc_sentinel_sites_2021_expansion.csv")
)

pre2015_only <- setdiff(names(cfg$provinces_pre2015), cfg$drc_provinces)

registry_table <- pairs_in |>
  mutate(
    file = if_else(
      sentinel_site %in% registry$sentinel_site,
      registry$file[match(sentinel_site, registry$sentinel_site)],
      "drc_sentinel_sites_26.csv"
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(Network = network) |>
  summarise(
    Sites = n(),
    Provinces = n_distinct(province),
    `Province names` = if_else(
      any(province %in% pre2015_only),
      paste0("pre-2015 (e.g. ",
             paste(head(intersect(province, pre2015_only), 2), collapse = ", "),
             ")"),
      "post-2015"
    ),
    `Sites read from` = paste(unique(file), collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

kable(registry_table, align = "lrrll")
```

> **Takeaway.** The geocoder works from one registry of `r nrow(registry)` sites: `r sum(registry$file == "drc_sentinel_sites_26.csv")` from the extractor plus `r sum(registry$file != "drc_sentinel_sites_26.csv")` from the 2021 file. The `r net_size[["2003_2005"]]` original sites keep their pre-2015 province in the pairs file, so each network is analysed on the map it was set up under.

# Geocoding the sites and DPS offices {#sec-geocoding}

**Why.** The registry holds names, not coordinates. An earlier, Google-only version reported every site as found, yet it placed Mikalayi (Kasaï-Central) on a business in Kinshasa about 700 km away. The rule since then is that **a wrong coordinate is worse than a missing one**. Each point is now geocoded independently by every source, an answer is kept only if it passes a strict quality gate, and the sources' answers are compared with each other:

- **Providers:** `r paste(names(Filter(\(p) p$enabled, cfg$providers)), collapse = ", ")` (Nominatim and Photon both serve OpenStreetMap). `r paste(names(Filter(\(p) !p$enabled, cfg$providers)), collapse = ", ")` is switched off until it has an account.
- **Query ladder:** `r nrow(cfg$ladders$sentinel_site)` queries per point, from the most specific (the health zone, pinned to its province) to the loosest (the name alone, anywhere in the DRC). A provider stops at the first answer the gate accepts.
- **Quality gate.** A candidate is rejected outright if:
  - it is the centroid of an administrative area rather than a place;
  - it is a street, river or railway;
  - it lies outside the DRC's bounding box;
  - it falls in a different province from the expected one;
  - its name similarity is below `r cfg$gate$similarity_floor`;
  - its name carries a different number (Maluku 1 is not Maluku 2).

  Softer problems only lower the confidence tier (high, medium or low).
- **Two coordinate sets** are chosen from the same answers: `google_first` (`r paste(cfg$chains$google_first, collapse = " → ")`) and `open_first` (`r paste(cfg$chains$open_first, collapse = " → ")`). Only open-source coordinates may be published, because Google's terms forbid showing its coordinates on a non-Google map.
- **Cross-check:** each kept point is compared with every other source. It *agrees* when another family of sources is within `r cfg$crosscheck$agree_km` km. Anything short of a confirmed high-confidence point goes to a person for review.
- **Manual overrides:** a reviewed point can be pinned in `manual_overrides.csv`. Pinned points win over every provider.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false" title="Where it lives"}
- **Workflow:** `geocoding/pipeline/drc-geocoding-workflow.qmd` (sentinel sites) and `drc-dps-site-pairs.qmd` (DPS offices), both built on `config.R`, `providers.R` and `geocode-functions.R`
- **Reads:** the two site files from §1, `geocoding/input/drc_dps.csv`, `manual_overrides.csv`; the response cache in `geocoding/cache/`
- **Writes:** `geocoding/output/drc_sentinel_sites_geocoded_{google_first,open_first}.csv`, `drc_dps_geocoded_{…}.csv`, `*_by_provider.csv`, `*_review_{…}.csv`, `*_provider_stats.csv`
- **Tests:** `geocoding/pipeline/test-geocode-functions.R`, which replays recorded responses from `fixtures/`
:::

**Result: each provider on its own.** Each provider answers every point. GRID3 skips the free-text rungs, and the OpenStreetMap services skip the health-zone rung.

```{r}
#| label: providers
#| code-summary: "How this table is built"

by_site <- read_data("drc_geocoding_by_provider.csv", geo_out)
by_dps  <- read_data("drc_dps_by_provider.csv", geo_out)

provider_stats <- bind_rows(
  read_data("drc_geocoding_provider_stats.csv", geo_out),
  read_data("drc_dps_provider_stats.csv", geo_out)
) |>
  group_by(provider) |>
  summarise(requests = sum(requests), cache_hits = sum(cache_hits))

n_sites <- n_distinct(by_site$site_id)
n_dps   <- n_distinct(by_dps$dps_id)

provider_table <- by_site |>
  group_by(provider) |>
  summarise(
    sites = sum(geocode_status != "failed"),
    tiers = sprintf(
      "%d / %d / %d",
      sum(confidence == "high"),
      sum(confidence == "medium"),
      sum(confidence == "low")
    )
  ) |>
  left_join(
    by_dps |>
      group_by(provider) |>
      summarise(dps = sum(geocode_status != "failed")),
    by = "provider"
  ) |>
  left_join(provider_stats, by = "provider") |>
  arrange(match(provider, names(cfg$providers)))

provider_table |>
  transmute(
    Provider = provider,
    `Source family` = vapply(provider, \(p) cfg$providers[[p]]$family, ""),
    `Sites placed` = sprintf("%d of %d", sites, n_sites),
    `High / medium / low` = tiers,
    `DPS offices placed` = sprintf("%d of %d", dps, n_dps),
    `Live requests (last run)` = requests,
    `Answers from cache` = cache_hits
  ) |>
  kable(align = "llrcrrr")
```

The last run sent `r sum(provider_table$requests)` live requests`r if (sum(provider_table$requests) == 0) ": every answer came from the cache" else "; the rest came from the cache"`. The cache is why the outputs can be re-rendered without spending Google quota.

**Result: the two coordinate sets.**

```{r}
#| label: chains
#| code-summary: "How this table is built"
#| results: hold

chains <- names(cfg$chains)

by_chain <- lapply(
  c(
    sites       = "drc_sentinel_sites_geocoded_%s.csv",
    site_review = "drc_geocoding_review_%s.csv",
    dps         = "drc_dps_geocoded_%s.csv",
    dps_review  = "drc_dps_review_%s.csv"
  ),
  \(pattern) bind_rows(lapply(chains, \(ch)
    read_data(sprintf(pattern, ch), geo_out) |> mutate(chain = ch)))
)

geocoded    <- by_chain$sites
site_review <- by_chain$site_review
dps_geo     <- by_chain$dps
dps_review  <- by_chain$dps_review

n_overrides <- nrow(read_data("manual_overrides.csv", geo_in)) +
  nrow(read_data("dps_manual_overrides.csv", geo_in))

geocoded |>
  group_by(Set = chain) |>
  summarise(
    `Sites placed` = sum(!is.na(latitude)),
    `Placed by` = {
      tb <- sort(table(geocode_status), decreasing = TRUE)
      paste(names(tb), tb, collapse = ", ")
    },
    `High / medium / low` = sprintf(
      "%d / %d / %d",
      sum(confidence == "high"),
      sum(confidence == "medium"),
      sum(confidence == "low")
    ),
    `Agree / disagree / single source` = sprintf(
      "%d / %d / %d",
      sum(crosscheck == "agree"),
      sum(crosscheck == "disagree"),
      sum(crosscheck == "single-source")
    )
  ) |>
  left_join(count(site_review, Set = chain, name = "Sites to review"), by = "Set") |>
  left_join(
    dps_geo |>
      group_by(Set = chain) |>
      summarise(`DPS placed` = sum(!is.na(latitude))),
    by = "Set"
  ) |>
  left_join(count(dps_review, Set = chain, name = "DPS to review"), by = "Set") |>
  mutate(across(ends_with("to review"), \(x) coalesce(x, 0L))) |>
  kable(align = "lrlcccrr")

# Distance between the two sets' point for each site (no coordinates shown)
both <- geocoded |>
  filter(!is.na(latitude)) |>
  select(chain, site_id, sentinel_site, latitude, longitude)

gap <- inner_join(
  filter(both, chain == "google_first"),
  filter(both, chain == "open_first"),
  by = c("site_id", "sentinel_site"),
  suffix = c("_g", "_o")
)

gap$km <- as.numeric(st_distance(
  st_as_sf(gap, coords = c("longitude_g", "latitude_g"), crs = 4326),
  st_as_sf(gap, coords = c("longitude_o", "latitude_o"), crs = 4326),
  by_element = TRUE
)) / 1000

widest <- slice_max(gap, km, n = 1)
widest_review_sets <- sum(
  chains %in% site_review$chain[site_review$site_id == widest$site_id]
)
widest_review_text <- if (widest_review_sets == length(chains)) {
  "the review list in both sets"
} else {
  sprintf("the review list in %d of the %d sets", widest_review_sets, length(chains))
}

mikalayi <- geocoded |>
  filter(chain == "open_first", sentinel_site == "Mikalayi")
```

How far do open sources get without Google? They placed `r sum(geocoded$chain == "open_first" & !is.na(geocoded$latitude))` of `r n_sites` sites and `r sum(dps_geo$chain == "open_first" & !is.na(dps_geo$latitude))` of `r n_dps` DPS offices. The two sets put a site a median `r sprintf("%.1f", median(gap$km))` km apart, and `r sum(gap$km <= cfg$crosscheck$agree_km)` of `r nrow(gap)` sites lie within `r cfg$crosscheck$agree_km` km. The widest gap is `r widest$sentinel_site` at `r sprintf("%.0f", widest$km)` km, and it is on `r widest_review_text`. Mikalayi, the site that started all this, is now placed by `r mikalayi$geocode_status` with `r mikalayi$confidence` confidence, and the cross-check says *`r mikalayi$crosscheck`* (`r mikalayi$crosscheck_note`). The override files hold `r n_overrides` pinned points.

**Result: the open-source map.**

```{r}
#| label: map-data
#| code-summary: "How the map data are prepared"

stage_label <- c(
  "2003_2005" = "Historical (2003–2005)",
  "2014" = "Added in 2014",
  "2021_expansion" = "Proposed in 2021"
)
stage_colours <- setNames(c("#8E44AD", "#E64B35", "#F4A300"), stage_label)

# Open-source coordinates only; the guard drops any row Google had to fill
sites_open <- read_data("drc_sentinel_sites_geocoded_open_first.csv", geo_out)
review_open <- read_data("drc_geocoding_review_open_first.csv", geo_out)
pairs_open <- read_data("drc_dps_site_pairs_open_first.csv", geo_out)

# A site's colour is the network it entered; network names sort by year
entered <- pairs_open |>
  group_by(site_id) |>
  summarise(network = min(network))

map_sites <- sites_open |>
  filter(geocode_status != "google", !is.na(latitude)) |>
  left_join(entered, by = "site_id") |>
  mutate(
    stage = stage_label[network],
    review = site_id %in% review_open$site_id
  )

# Several DPS share a seat (pre-2015 and current), so one marker per seat
map_dps <- read_data("drc_dps_geocoded_open_first.csv", geo_out) |>
  filter(geocode_status != "google", !is.na(latitude)) |>
  group_by(chef_lieu, latitude, longitude) |>
  summarise(
    dps = paste(dps, collapse = " / "),
    source = first(geocode_status),
    confidence = first(confidence),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Province outlines dissolved from the GRID3 health zones, simplified to
# about 1 km so the map stays readable without basemap tiles
old_s2 <- sf_use_s2(FALSE)
provinces <- st_read(
  "GRID3_COD_health_zones/GRID3_COD_health_zones_v9_0.shp",
  quiet = TRUE
) |>
  st_make_valid() |>
  group_by(province) |>
  summarise(.groups = "drop") |>
  st_simplify(dTolerance = 0.01, preserveTopology = TRUE)
invisible(sf_use_s2(old_s2))
```

::: {.column-page-right}

```{r}
#| label: map
#| code-summary: "How the map is drawn (adapted from drc-geocoding-workflow.qmd)"

pal <- colorFactor(unname(stage_colours), levels = names(stage_colours))

map <- leaflet(height = 650) |>
  addTiles(group = "OpenStreetMap") |>
  addPolygons(
    data = provinces,
    group = "Province boundaries",
    color = "#555555", weight = 1.2, fill = FALSE,
    label = ~province
  )

for (s in names(stage_colours)) {
  map <- map |>
    addCircleMarkers(
      data = filter(map_sites, stage == s),
      lng = ~longitude, lat = ~latitude,
      group = s,
      radius = 8,
      color = stage_colours[[s]],
      weight = ~if_else(review, 3, 1.5),
      fillColor = stage_colours[[s]],
      fillOpacity = ~if_else(review, 0, 0.85),
      label = ~sentinel_site,
      popup = ~paste0(
        "<b>", sentinel_site, "</b><br>",
        "<b>Province:</b> ", province, "<br>",
        "<b>Network:</b> ", stage, "<br>",
        "<b>Provider:</b> ", geocode_status, "<br>",
        "<b>Confidence:</b> ", confidence, "<br>",
        "<b>Cross-check:</b> ", crosscheck,
        if_else(review, "<br><i>Sent to review</i>", "")
      )
    )
}

map |>
  addCircleMarkers(
    data = map_dps,
    lng = ~longitude, lat = ~latitude,
    group = "DPS offices",
    radius = 5, color = "white", weight = 1.5,
    fillColor = "#1F2D3D", fillOpacity = 1,
    label = ~dps,
    popup = ~paste0(
      "<b>", dps, "</b><br>",
      "<b>Seat:</b> ", chef_lieu, "<br>",
      "<b>Provider:</b> ", source, "<br>",
      "<b>Confidence:</b> ", confidence
    )
  ) |>
  addLegend(
    "bottomright",
    colors = c(unname(stage_colours), "#1F2D3D"),
    labels = c(names(stage_colours), "DPS office"),
    title = "Open-source points",
    opacity = 1
  ) |>
  addLayersControl(
    overlayGroups = c(names(stage_colours), "DPS offices", "Province boundaries"),
    options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)
  )
```

:::

*Map: `open_first` coordinates only. The open providers (GRID3, Nominatim, Photon) placed `r nrow(map_sites)` of the `r n_sites` sentinel sites and `r nrow(map_dps)` DPS seats. Hollow circles are the `r sum(map_sites$review)` sites the cross-check sent to review. The accessibility analysis itself used the `google_first` coordinates, which Google's terms do not allow on a non-Google map. Province outlines come from GRID3 health zones v9.0, simplified.*

```{r}
#| label: tests
#| code-summary: "How the test suite is run while rendering"

test_file <- "geocoding/pipeline/test-geocode-functions.R"

# Offline by design: recorded responses only, no API keys, temp files only
test_lines <- system(
  sprintf(
    "cd geocoding/pipeline && R_LIBS=%s %s test-geocode-functions.R 2>&1",
    shQuote(paste(.libPaths(), collapse = ":")),
    shQuote(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"))
  ),
  intern = TRUE
)

total <- grep("PASSED:", test_lines, value = TRUE)
passed <- as.integer(sub(".*PASSED: *([0-9]+).*", "\\1", total))
failed <- as.integer(sub(".*FAILED: *([0-9]+).*", "\\1", total))

n_ok_calls <- sum(grepl("^\\s*ok\\(", readLines(test_file)))
n_fixtures <- length(list.files("geocoding/pipeline/fixtures"))

test_sections <- tibble(line = test_lines) |>
  mutate(section = if_else(startsWith(line, "== "), gsub("^== | ==$", "", line), NA)) |>
  fill(section) |>
  filter(!is.na(section)) |>
  mutate(section = factor(section, levels = unique(section))) |>
  group_by(Section = section) |>
  summarise(
    Passed = sum(grepl("^\\s+PASS", line)),
    Failed = sum(grepl("^\\s+FAIL", line))
  )
```

**Result: the offline test suite.** The gate is tested against real responses: Google's are copied in as parsed rows, and `r n_fixtures` open-provider responses are stored verbatim in `fixtures/`. The test file makes `r n_ok_calls` `ok()` checks in `r nrow(test_sections)` sections. This page ran it while rendering, with no network and no API key: **`r passed` passed, `r failed` failed**.`r if (passed + failed > n_ok_calls) " The live count is higher than the number of calls because a loop repeats some checks." else ""`

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" title="Test results by section"}
```{r}
#| echo: false
kable(test_sections, align = "lrr")
```
:::

> **Takeaway.** Open sources alone place `r nrow(map_sites)` of `r n_sites` sites, and the two coordinate sets agree within `r cfg$crosscheck$agree_km` km for `r sum(gap$km <= cfg$crosscheck$agree_km)` of them. The `r sum(site_review$chain == "open_first")` sites that are not confirmed go to a person rather than straight into the analysis.

# DPS–site pairs and analysis inputs {#sec-pairs}

**Why.** Supervision is a journey from a DPS office to a site, so each site is paired with the DPS that supervises it, network by network. The pairing step checks that every pair lies inside what its province became in 2015, so an old-province pair can't drift into the wrong region. A second script then writes the pairs in the layout the analysis scripts read.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false" title="Where it lives"}
- **Scripts:** `geocoding/pipeline/drc-dps-site-pairs.qmd` with `build_pairs()` in `pairs-functions.R`; then `build_walking_inputs.R` at the repo root
- **Reads:** `geocoding/input/drc_dps_site_pairs.csv` (network, province, DPS, site) and the geocoded points from §2
- **Writes:** `geocoding/output/drc_dps_site_pairs_{google_first,open_first}.csv`; then `output/dps_11.csv`, `ss_11.csv`, `dps_26.csv`, `ss_26.csv`, `network_51/ss_51.csv` and `network_51/missing_2021_site.csv` (from `google_first`)
:::

::: {.panel-tabset}

# Accessibility surfaces {#sec-surfaces}

**Why.** To ask "how much of the country is within reach?" we need travel time from every place, not just between pairs of points. Three ideas do the work:

- A **friction surface** is a Malaria Atlas Project (MAP) raster that gives, for each ~1 km cell, the minutes needed to cross it. It comes in a walking-only and a motorised version (2020).
- A **transition layer** turns that raster into a network: each cell is linked to its `r unique(model_cfg$directions)` neighbours, weighted by how easy the move is, and corrected for the curvature of the Earth.
- **Cumulative cost** (`accCost`) then gives, for every cell, the least travel time to the nearest of a set of starting points: the sentinel sites, or the DPS offices.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false" title="Where it lives"}
- **Script:** `R/02_accessibility.R`
- **Reads:** `output/ss_*.csv`, `output/dps_*.csv`; the MAP friction surfaces, downloaded once with `malariaAtlas` and cached as `output/friction_*.tif` with their transition layers `output/transition_*.rds`
- **Writes:** `output/unified/accessibility_*.tif` (`r nrow(validation)` rasters), Figures 2, 3, S1 and S2, `Table_accessibility_validation.csv`
- **Coverage table:** computed from those rasters by `R/05` (§7), `Table_spatial_accessibility_summary.csv`
:::

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| filename: "R/02_accessibility.R — prepare_transition() and calculate_accessibility()"
#| code: !expr 'c(excerpt("R/02_accessibility.R", "    fr <- malariaAtlas::getRaster(", "    stopifnot("), "", "    # ⋯", "", excerpt("R/02_accessibility.R", "    tr <- gdistance::transition(", "    stopifnot("), "", "    # ⋯", "", excerpt("R/02_accessibility.R", "    # Cost is in minutes; convert to hours", "    source_hours <-"))'
```

**Result.** Travel time to the nearest sentinel site (main results) and to the nearest DPS office (supplementary figures in the report). Click a map to enlarge it.

::: {.column-page-right}
::: {.panel-tabset}

## Walking → nearest site

![Motorised travel time to the nearest sentinel site, for the three configurations. `output/unified/FigureS2_motorized_nearest_sentinel_sites.png`](output/unified/FigureS2_motorized_nearest_sentinel_sites.png){fig-alt="Motorised accessibility to the nearest sentinel site"}

## Walking → nearest DPS

![Walking-only travel time to the nearest DPS office, under the historical and current DPS configurations. `output/unified/Figure2_walking_accessibility_final.png`](output/unified/Figure2_walking_accessibility_final.png){fig-alt="Walking accessibility to the nearest DPS office"}

## Motorised → nearest DPS

![Motorised travel time to the nearest DPS office, under the historical and current DPS configurations. `output/unified/Figure3_motorized_accessibility_final.png`](output/unified/Figure3_motorized_accessibility_final.png){fig-alt="Motorised accessibility to the nearest DPS office"}

:::
:::

```{r}
#| label: coverage
#| code-summary: "How this table is built"
#| results: hold

walk_limit  <- 24
motor_limit <- 6

headline <- coverage |>
  filter(
    (mode == "walking" & threshold_hours == walk_limit) |
      (mode == "motorized" & threshold_hours == motor_limit)
  ) |>
  select(network, mode, percent_modelled_area) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = mode, values_from = percent_modelled_area)

dps_coverage <- read_data("Table_dps_spatial_accessibility_summary.csv")

stopifnot(all(
  (dps_coverage$mode == "walking" & dps_coverage$threshold_hours == walk_limit) |
    (dps_coverage$mode == "motorized" & dps_coverage$threshold_hours == motor_limit)
))

dps_headline <- dps_coverage |>
  select(dps_offices = network, mode, coverage_percent) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = mode, values_from = coverage_percent,
              names_prefix = "dps_")

# Each configuration's DPS set is the set of offices its journeys start from
coverage_table <- journeys |>
  filter(mode == "walking") |>
  group_by(network) |>
  summarise(sites = n(), dps_offices = n_distinct(dps_office)) |>
  left_join(headline, by = "network") |>
  left_join(dps_headline, by = "dps_offices")

coverage_table |>
  transmute(
    Configuration = paste(network, "sites"),
    `DPS offices` = dps_offices,
    `≤ 24 h walk to a site (%)` = walking,
    `≤ 6 h motorised to a site (%)` = motorized,
    `≤ 24 h walk to a DPS (%)` = dps_walking,
    `≤ 6 h motorised to a DPS (%)` = dps_motorized
  ) |>
  kable(digits = 1, align = "lrrrrr")

cov_walk  <- setNames(coverage_table$walking, coverage_table$network)
cov_motor <- setNames(coverage_table$motorized, coverage_table$network)
```

All `r nrow(validation)` rasters passed the check that every starting point has a travel time of zero (`r sum(validation$zero_hour_origins)` of `r sum(validation$origins)` origins, with `r sum(validation$missing_values)` missing values). The coverage is the share of the modelled land area, not of the population.

> **Takeaway.** Within `r walk_limit` walking hours of a site, coverage rises from `r sprintf("%.1f", cov_walk[["11"]])`% to `r sprintf("%.1f", cov_walk[["26"]])`% and `r sprintf("%.1f", cov_walk[["51"]])`% of the country. Within `r motor_limit` motorised hours it rises from `r sprintf("%.1f", cov_motor[["11"]])`% to `r sprintf("%.1f", cov_motor[["26"]])`% and `r sprintf("%.1f", cov_motor[["51"]])`%. Even with the 2021 proposal, `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 - cov_walk[["51"]])`% of the land is more than a day's walk from a site.

# DPS → assigned-site travel and routes {#sec-travel}

**Why.** Supervision depends on the journey from each DPS office to *its own* sites, not to whichever office is nearest. The model finds the **least-cost path**, the route through the transition layer with the smallest total travel time, and reports its time. For walking it also traces that path to measure its length in kilometres.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false" title="Where it lives"}
- **Scripts:** `R/03_assigned_travel_time.R` (times), `R/04_walking_routes.R` (walking routes)
- **Reads:** `output/dps_*.csv`, `output/ss_*.csv`, `output/network_51/ss_51.csv`; the cached transition layers
- **Writes:** `output/unified/Table_assigned_travel_times.csv` (+ summary, QC and `matrices/`), `walking_route_distances.csv`, `walking_routes.gpkg`
- **Reuse:** by default `06_run_analysis.R` keeps the validated travel-time table, and `R/04` keeps the existing routes. `run_analysis(full_rebuild = TRUE)` recomputes both.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset}

## R/03: travel times

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| filename: "R/03_assigned_travel_time.R — calculate_network()"
#| code: !expr 'excerpt("R/03_assigned_travel_time.R", "  # Result: minutes from each DPS to every site", "  # Save full DPS-to-site matrix")'
```

## R/04: walking routes

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| filename: "R/04_walking_routes.R — calculate_routes()"
#| code: !expr 'c(excerpt("R/04_walking_routes.R", "      path <- gdistance::shortestPath(", "      path_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(path)"), "", "      # ⋯", "", excerpt("R/04_walking_routes.R", "      # Geodesic length of the modelled walking route", "      route_status <- \"calculated\""))'
```

:::

**Result.** The table and Figure 4 show both modes, so there is no tab to switch.

```{r}
#| label: travel
#| code-summary: "How this table is built"
#| results: hold

journey_table <- journeys |>
  select(network, stage, province, sentinel_site, dps_office,
         straight_km, mode, travel_hours) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = mode, values_from = travel_hours) |>
  left_join(
    routes |> select(network, province, sentinel_site, walking_route_km),
    by = c("network", "province", "sentinel_site")
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(journey_table) == nrow(journeys) / 2,
  !anyNA(journey_table$walking_route_km)
)

historical <- journey_table$sentinel_site[journey_table$network == 11]

groups <- bind_rows(
  journey_table |> filter(network == 11) |>
    mutate(group = "2003–2005 network"),
  journey_table |> filter(network == 26, !sentinel_site %in% historical) |>
    mutate(group = "2014 additions"),
  journey_table |> filter(network == 26) |>
    mutate(group = "2014 network"),
  journey_table |> filter(network == 51, stage == "2021 proposed") |>
    mutate(group = "2021 proposed additions"),
  journey_table |> filter(network == 51) |>
    mutate(group = "2021 proposed network")
) |>
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = unique(group)))

group_summary <- groups |>
  group_by(Configuration = group) |>
  summarise(
    Journeys = n(),
    walk_median = median(walking),
    `Walking h, median (IQR)` = sprintf(
      "%.1f (%.1f–%.1f)",
      median(walking), quantile(walking, 0.25), quantile(walking, 0.75)
    ),
    `Walking > 24 h` = sum(walking > 24),
    `Motorised h, median (IQR)` = sprintf(
      "%.1f (%.1f–%.1f)",
      median(motorized), quantile(motorized, 0.25), quantile(motorized, 0.75)
    ),
    `Motorised ≥ 2 h` = sum(motorized >= 2),
    `Walking route km, median (IQR)` = sprintf(
      "%.0f (%.0f–%.0f)",
      median(walking_route_km),
      quantile(walking_route_km, 0.25),
      quantile(walking_route_km, 0.75)
    )
  )

group_summary |>
  select(-walk_median) |>
  kable(align = "lrrrrrr")

# Repeated journeys across networks share a route_id
distinct_routes <- routes |> distinct(route_id, .keep_all = TRUE)
longest <- slice_max(distinct_routes, walking_route_km, n = 1)

adds_2014 <- filter(group_summary, Configuration == "2014 additions")
adds_2014_colocated <- sum(groups$group == "2014 additions" & groups$straight_km == 0)
adds_2021 <- filter(group_summary, Configuration == "2021 proposed additions")
```

![Modelled walking and motorised travel time from each DPS office to its assigned sites, by configuration (drawn by `R/05`). `output/unified/Figure4_assigned_travel_time_distributions.png`](output/unified/Figure4_assigned_travel_time_distributions.png){fig-alt="Boxplots of assigned travel times by network and mode" width="80%"}

The `r nrow(routes)` walking-route records cover `r nrow(distinct_routes)` distinct DPS–site journeys, because the later networks repeat earlier ones. The longest is `r sprintf("%.1f", longest$walking_route_km)` km, from the `r longest$dps_office` DPS office to `r longest$sentinel_site`. `r sum(distinct_routes$route_status == "same_raster_cell")` journeys have zero length, because the DPS and the site fall in the same 1 km cell.

> **Takeaway.** The `r adds_2021$Journeys` proposed 2021 sites sit a median `r sprintf("%.1f", adds_2021$walk_median)` walking hours from their DPS, against `r sprintf("%.1f", adds_2014$walk_median)` h for the `r adds_2014$Journeys` added in 2014, `r adds_2014_colocated` of which share their DPS's coordinates. `r adds_2021[["Walking > 24 h"]]` of them need more than a day on foot. `r if (adds_2021$walk_median > adds_2014$walk_median) "The new sites widen coverage, but they make supervision journeys longer." else "The new sites widen coverage without lengthening supervision journeys."`

**Why.** `R/05` turns the rasters and journey tables into the comparisons the report uses: how much land each configuration reaches, how walking and motorised times relate, and how much coverage each added site buys. `06_run_analysis.R` runs the scripts in order and checks that every expected output exists.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false" title="Where it lives"}

- **Writes:** `Table_spatial_accessibility_summary.csv`, `Table_dps_spatial_accessibility_summary.csv`, `Table_walking_vs_motorized.csv` and other summaries; Figures 4, 5 and 6; poster copies in `output/poster/`

```{r}
modes <- read_data("Table_walking_vs_motorized.csv")
moving <- filter(modes, motorized > 0)

gain <- tibble(
  stage = c("2014", "2021"),
  walking = c(
    (cov_walk[["26"]] - cov_walk[["11"]]) / adds_2014$Journeys,
    (cov_walk[["51"]] - cov_walk[["26"]]) / adds_2021$Journeys
  ),
  motorized = c(
    (cov_motor[["26"]] - cov_motor[["11"]]) / adds_2014$Journeys,

)
```

## Walking vs motorised (Figure 5)

![Walking against motorised travel time for every assigned journey; the dashed line marks equal times. `output/unified/Figure5_walking_vs_motorized.png`](output/unified/Figure5_walking_vs_motorized.png){fig-alt="Scatter plots of walking versus motorised travel time by network"}

Motorised travel is slower than walking for `r sum(modes$motorized_longer)` of `r nrow(modes)` journeys. For journeys of non-zero length, walking takes a median `r sprintf("%.1f", median(moving$walking / moving$motorized))` times as long as motorised travel.

## Area covered (Figure 6)

![Share of the modelled DRC area within 24 walking hours and 6 motorised hours of the nearest sentinel site. `output/unified/Figure6_spatial_accessibility_comparison.png`](output/unified/Figure6_spatial_accessibility_comparison.png){fig-alt="Bar charts of area covered by each network" width="85%"}

Per added site, the 2014 additions bought `r sprintf("%.2f", gain$walking[1])` percentage points of walking coverage each, and the 2021 proposals `r sprintf("%.2f", gain$walking[2])`. For motorised coverage the figures are `r sprintf("%.2f", gain$motorized[1])` and `r sprintf("%.2f", gain$motorized[2])`.

This page runs that block, which only calls `file.exists()` and `file.info()`, exactly as written in the script. The whole block, including the two file lists, is in *View Source*.

```{r}
#| eval: false
```

```{r}
#| label: runner-check
#| code-summary: "How the check is run"

runner <- new.env()
runner$out_dir <- out_dir

eval(
  parse(text = excerpt(
    "06_run_analysis.R",
    "  # Verify final outputs",
    "  print(status, row.names = FALSE)"
  )),
  envir = runner
)

runner$status |>
  transmute(
    Folder = dirname(output),

  ) |>

```

> **Takeaway.** `r sum(runner$status$exists)` of `r nrow(runner$status)` expected outputs are present (`r sprintf("%.1f", sum(runner$status$size_mb))` MB). Each site proposed in 2021 buys `r if (gain$walking[2] < gain$walking[1]) "less" else "more"` new coverage than one added in 2014: `r sprintf("%.2f", gain$walking[2])` against `r sprintf("%.2f", gain$walking[1])` percentage points of walking coverage.

# Reproduce it {#sec-reproduce}

The commands for this pipeline, pulled from the *Commands* block of `AGENTS.md` and put in pipeline order: registry, geocoding, pairs, analysis inputs, analysis, report and poster, then the offline tests. The provider benchmark and the commands for the separate Kasaï-Central documents are left out. Requests only go out for answers not already in the cache, and the default analysis run reuses the validated travel times.

```{bash}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
#| filename: "AGENTS.md — Commands, in pipeline order"
#| code: !expr 'c(excerpt("AGENTS.md", "once per shell, from the repo root", "# Geocoding tests"), "", excerpt("AGENTS.md", "# Rebuild the 26-site input", "# Accessibility inputs"), "", excerpt("AGENTS.md", "# Geocoding run.", "# Provider benchmark"), "", excerpt("AGENTS.md", "# Accessibility inputs", strrep("\x60", 3)), "", excerpt("AGENTS.md", "# Geocoding tests", "# Geocoding run."))'
```

**The deliverables** (keep these three files next to this page when copying it to another laptop):

- [Final report (HTML)](ecr_final_report.html)
- [Final report (PDF)](ecr_final_report.pdf)
- [Poster (PDF)](ecr_poster.pdf)
